You are fixing a bug in the Python repository in the current working directory. The bug and the required behavior are described below. Read the relevant source files, make the necessary code edits to the source (do NOT edit the tests), and use the shell to run the tests to confirm your fix. Keep changes minimal.

ISSUE:
word_count(text) should count words separated by any whitespace, collapsing runs of spaces and ignoring leading/trailing spaces. Currently word_count('  a   b  ') returns the wrong number because it splits on a single space and counts empty strings between them. It must return 2, while word_count('a b c') must still return 3.

The test suite lives in tests/. You can run it with: python -m pytest -q
When the tests pass, you are done.

We need to modify word_count to split on any whitespace and collapse runs. Use text.split() default splits on any whitespace and removes empties. So change to return len(text.split()). Also handle leading/trailing spaces fine.

Implement edit.
Implemented proper word counting by using `text.split()` which handles any whitespace and collapses consecutive spaces. All tests now pass.
